metadata.description: PPO (paper A, 2017) extends TRPO (paper B, 2015) by replacing TRPO's hard KL trust-region constraint and second-order conjugate-gradient update with a first-order clipped surrogate objective $L^{CLIP}$ optimized via multiple SGD epochs. PPO inherits TRPO's importance-sampled surrogate $L^{CPI}$, the probability-ratio formulation, and the trust-region motivation, but trades the constrained second-order machinery for a cheaper clipping/penalty mechanism that is easier to implement and tune.

matches.explanation: PPO names the vanilla policy-gradient surrogate $L^{PG}=\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[\log\pi_\theta(a_t|s_t)\hat A_t]$ as a starting point. TRPO never introduces this loss explicitly — its development goes from $\eta(\pi)$ directly to the importance-sampled local surrogate $L_\pi(\tilde\pi)$ (DP243.5). No direct counterpart in paper B.

PPO defines the probability ratio $r_t(\theta)=\pi_\theta/\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}$ as a named, first-class object so it can drive the clip operator. TRPO uses the same ratio implicitly inside its importance-sampled subproblem ProbP243.3 but never elevates it to a standalone definition.

PPO's Conservative Policy Iteration surrogate $L^{CPI}(\theta)=\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[r_t(\theta)\hat A_t]$ is the sample / importance-sampled form of TRPO's local surrogate $L_\pi(\tilde\pi)=\eta(\pi)+\sum_s\rho_\pi(s)\sum_a\tilde\pi(a|s)A_\pi(s,a)$. They play the same role (first-order surrogate around $\theta_{\text{old}}$, ignoring state-visitation drift) and PPO explicitly cites Kakade--Langford as the origin. Different but equivalent renderings (state-form vs.\ ratio-form).

The clipped surrogate $L^{CLIP}$ is the central new contribution of PPO and has no counterpart in TRPO; TRPO controls policy change through a hard KL constraint rather than a clipped probability ratio.

PPO's KL-penalized surrogate $L^{KLPEN}=\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[r_t\hat A_t-\beta\,\mathrm{KL}]$ is the same minorization form as TRPO's KL-penalty inequality $\eta(\tilde\pi)\ge L_\pi(\tilde\pi)-C\,D^{max}_{KL}(\pi,\tilde\pi)$ (EP243.4) and the corresponding penalized policy-iteration scheme AP243.1. The penalty coefficient $\beta$ in PPO is adapted online; TRPO's $C$ is the analytic constant $4\epsilon\gamma/(1-\gamma)^2$.

The combined loss $L^{CLIP+VF+S}$ adds a value-function squared error and an entropy bonus to support shared actor-critic networks; TRPO has no such joint loss because its actor update is a constrained second-order step independent of the critic.

PPO's ProbP242.1 (max surrogate s.t.\ $\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[\mathrm{KL}]\le\delta$) is exactly TRPO's trust-region problem. ProbP243.1 is the average-KL form used in practice and ProbP243.2 the max-KL form; PPO cites this constrained problem as TRPO's, with origin tagged Schulman 2015b. Many-to-many because TRPO splits the constraint into max-KL and average-KL variants.

PPO's ProbP242.2 is the unconstrained KL-penalized form $\max_\theta\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[r_t\hat A_t-\beta\,\mathrm{KL}]$, which is precisely the maximization of TRPO's KL-divergence policy improvement bound EP243.4 (Lagrangian relaxation of the trust-region problem). Cross-type (problem ↔ equation) but the mathematics is identical: PPO frames the inequality as the objective of an optimization problem.
The adaptive KL penalty algorithm is original to PPO: TRPO's $C$ is fixed analytically and TRPO never adapts a penalty coefficient (it instead enforces a hard constraint via line search).

PPO's Algorithm 1 (parallel actors, $K$ epochs of minibatch SGD on the surrogate) and TRPO's practical algorithm AP243.2 are both iterative on-policy update loops that collect samples, build a surrogate, and update $\theta_{\text{old}}$. They differ fundamentally in the inner update (first-order SGD vs.\ conjugate-gradient + line search with KL constraint) — analogous role, different machinery, which is the central EXT relationship of this pair.

PPO's AP242.3 is its short description of TRPO (cited as Schulman 2015b); it corresponds exactly to paper B's TRPO algorithm AP243.2 (conjugate-gradient on the linearized objective with a quadratic KL approximation). Paper A's node is origin=external, paper B's is origin=paper — a textbook external-vs-paper alignment that supports the EXT relation.

PPO's only proof argues that $L^{CLIP}$ is a pessimistic lower bound on $L^{CPI}$. TRPO's proofs (PP243.1, PP243.2) establish the policy-improvement bound for $\eta$ in terms of $L_\pi$ and $D^{max}_{KL}$, a different claim entirely.

TRPO's expected discounted return $\eta(\pi)=\mathbb{E}[\sum_t\gamma^t r(s_t)]$ is foundational RL background. PPO uses returns implicitly through advantages and value functions but never names $\eta$ as a definition.
Discounted state-visitation $\rho_\pi(s)$ underpins TRPO's local-surrogate construction and the proof of Theorem 1. PPO operates entirely in trajectory-sample space and never names this measure.

TRPO's named average/max KL definitions $D^{max}_{KL}$ and $\bar D^\rho_{KL}$ correspond to PPO's informal usage of KL inside $L^{KLPEN}$ (DP242.6) and inside the adaptive-penalty algorithm (AP242.1), where $d=\hat{\mathbb{E}}_t[\mathrm{KL}]$ is the empirical analogue of TRPO's $\bar D^\rho_{KL}$. PPO does not separately define the KL operator, so this is a definition-vs-usage correspondence.
$\alpha$-coupled policy pair is an auxiliary construct inside TRPO's coupling proof of Theorem 1. PPO does not engage with the policy-improvement-bound proof and has no counterpart.
Mean advantage $\bar A(s)$ is a proof-internal quantity in TRPO's coupling argument with no counterpart in PPO.

TRPO's state-form rewrite $\eta(\tilde\pi)=\eta(\pi)+\sum_s\rho_{\tilde\pi}(s)\sum_a\tilde\pi(a|s)A_\pi(s,a)$ is the exact identity that motivates both $L^{CPI}$ (paper A's DP242.4) and the KL-penalty bound. PPO uses $L^{CPI}$ directly without restating the underlying identity, so there is no explicit counterpart in paper A.

TRPO's main theoretical result — the policy-improvement bound $\eta(\pi_{\text{new}})\ge L_{\pi_{\text{old}}}(\pi_{\text{new}})-\frac{4\epsilon\gamma}{(1-\gamma)^2}\alpha^2$ — has no counterpart in PPO, which abandons the bound-driven design in favor of a heuristic clip.
Bound on mean advantage under coupled policies (Lemma 2) is internal to TRPO's coupling proof; PPO has no analogous lemma.
Bound on state-distribution shift (Lemma 3) is internal to TRPO's coupling proof; PPO has no analogous lemma.
TRPO's coupling proof of Theorem 1 has no PPO counterpart; PPO does not prove a policy-improvement bound.
TRPO's perturbation-theory / resolvent proof of Theorem 1 has no PPO counterpart.

TRPO's importance-sampled subproblem with average-KL constraint is the bridge from theory to a sample-based update. PPO drops the constraint entirely, so there is no analogue subproblem in paper A — only the constrained ProbP242.1/ProbP242.2 which match TRPO's higher-level problems.

Single-path sampling is a TRPO-specific Monte-Carlo scheme for $\hat Q$. PPO uses GAE-based advantage estimates inside its actor-critic loop and does not adopt single-path rollouts as a named procedure.
Vine sampling is TRPO-specific (rollout sets, $K$ actions per state, common random numbers). PPO has no counterpart.
